'''Charles Walcott''' (born 1934) is an [[Ethology|ethologist]] and [[Emeritus|Professor Emeritus]] at [[Cornell University]].<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |title=Charles Walcott|url=https://nbb.cornell.edu/charles-walcott |access-date=2024-08-26 |website=nbb.cornell.edu}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2023-02-06 |title=With love and duty, retired academics give back to Cornell|url=https://nbb.cornell.edu/news/love-and-duty-retired-academics-give-back-cornell |access-date=2024-08-26 |website=nbb.cornell.edu |language=en}}</ref> He studied how spiders catch prey, as well as how [[Homing pigeon|pigeons home]].<ref>{{Cite news |last=Hauser |first=Christine |date=2019-12-10 |title=Someone Is Putting Cowboy Hats on Pigeons in Las Vegas |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2019/12/10/us/pigeons-cowboy-hats-las-vegas.html |access-date=2024-08-26 |work=The New York Times |language=en-US |issn=0362-4331}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |date=2024-05-26 |title=PR for pigeons: Woman's mission to give the birds a better image |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/uk-england-nottinghamshire-66604567 |access-date=2024-08-26 |work=BBC News |language=en-GB}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=Libby |first=Sam |date=1998-12-06 |title=When Homing Pigeons Don't Go Home Again |url=https://www.nytimes.com/1998/12/06/nyregion/when-homing-pigeons-don-t-go-home-again.html |access-date=2024-08-26 |work=The New York Times |language=en-US |issn=0362-4331}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=Vadukul |first=Alex |date=2012-02-04 |title=Rescuing the Birds Many Hate |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2012/02/05/nyregion/rescuing-the-birds-many-love-to-hate.html |access-date=2024-08-26 |work=The New York Times |language=en-US |issn=0362-4331}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=Rubenstein |first=Carin |date=2004-10-03 |title=ENVIRONMENT; Rousting Pigeons? It's Like Herding Cats |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2004/10/03/nyregion/environment-rousting-pigeons-its-like-herding-cats.html |access-date=2024-08-26 |work=The New York Times |language=en-US |issn=0362-4331}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last=Walcott |first=Charles |date=1996-01-01 |title=Pigeon Homing: Observations, Experiments and Confusions |url=http://dx.doi.org/10.1242/jeb.199.1.21 |journal=Journal of Experimental Biology |volume=199 |issue=1 |pages=21–27 |doi=10.1242/jeb.199.1.21 |issn=0022-0949|url-access=subscription }}</ref>

==Early life and education==
Walcott obtained his A.B. in [[biology]] in 1956 and his Ph.D. in [[zoology]] from Cornell in 1959.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=CV |url=https://cornell.app.box.com/s/dkgrrnxd4zunwtn08t6e9ajr13gvlbi8}}</ref>

==Career==
He worked as an assistant professor at [[Harvard University|Harvard]] from 1961 to 1965 and then at Tufts until 1967 and at [[SUNY Stony Brook]] until 1981. He then returned to Cornell as full professor, staying until his retirement in 2016. In this period he was the director (later [[Louis Agassiz Fuertes]] Director) of the [[Cornell Lab of Ornithology]] from 1981-1995, succeeded by [[John W. Fitzpatrick]],<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":1" /> and served as Dean of Faculty from 2003 to 2008 and as University Ombudsman.<ref name=":1" /><ref>{{Cite web |date=2023-02-06 |title=Charles Walcott |url=https://cals.cornell.edu/people/charles-walcott |access-date=2026-05-01 |website=College of Agriculture and Life Sciences, Cornell University |language=en}}</ref> He was elected as a fellow to the [[American Association for the Advancement of Science]] (AAAS) in 2018.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2018-11-27 |title=Nine faculty members elected AAAS fellows |url=https://nbb.cornell.edu/news/nine-faculty-members-elected-aaas-fellows |access-date=2024-08-26 |website=nbb.cornell.edu |language=en}}</ref>

He also worked as a producer of nature TV shows for children for [[WGBH Educational Foundation|WGBH]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Charles Walcott, PhD. |url=https://www.wgbh.org/people/charles-walcott-phd |access-date=2024-08-26 |website=GBH |language=en}}</ref><ref name=":0" />
